description: GitHub-managed injection-molding recipe (Einstellparameter / SOLL) for article housing-A on sgm-004. The five monitored bands below are the active tolerance bands behind the recipe_* constraints. Edit + push to GitHub -> the it-evaluator GithubRecipeSource picks the new bands up at runtime (no redeploy). The IST is read at the edge; the active band is resolved centrally from this file by (article x equipment x setup). --- 2026-07-12 (v3.2.0): kept in lockstep with recipe-sgm-004-default v3.3.0. mouldTempC SOLL 50 -> 85 degC, band [40,60] -> [80,90], toleranceSource -> 'norm' (BINDING): the mould temperature is a property of the RESIN, not of the article — the same PA66-GF30 needs 80-90 degC whether it is moulded into a housing or a bracket, so this band moves with the default recipe rather than staying behind as a contradiction that would resurrect the old, wrong 50 degC the moment this article-specific recipe ever won a match. The peak/hold pressure GATE doc-strings move from inCycle==true to phaseName==HOLD to match the corrected 'when' guards in the profile (the pressure BANDS themselves are article-specific and unchanged). NOTE: this recipe matches on article 'housing-A', which the real ERP never emits (its articles are codes like _V4_14-1300-017); the equipment-scoped default recipe is the one that is actually active on sgm-004. --- 2026-07-31 WAVE-3: hotrunnerTempC SOLL 230 -> 295 degC, band [223.5,236.5] -> [288.5,301.5], kept in lockstep with recipe-sgm-004-default (see that file for the full derivation). Short form: sgm-004's configured nozzle setpoint IS 295 degC (sim-v5 packages/machines-sgm/src/config.ts:337), hotrunnerTempC is published as nozzleC + normal(0,1.5) per cavity (machine.ts:1281-1283), and the consumer MEASURED mean 295.0 / range 289.9-300.5 over 6277 samples on 2026-07-31. The half-width +-6.5 is UNCHANGED — only the centre moved onto the machine spec. This band is corrected here for exactly the reason the mouldTempC paragraph above gives: this recipe never wins a match today, so the wrong number is inert RIGHT NOW, and that is precisely why it must not be left behind as a contradiction waiting to resurrect itself the moment the match fires. NOTE that the hot-runner temperature is NOT article-specific in the simulated plant: nozzleSetpointC is a per-machine config constant and LOAD_PROGRAM overrides only program / cycle time / mouldId (machine.ts:481-562), while the mould design records and mould library carry no temperature fields at all. So housing-A and bracket-B legitimately share one hot-runner SOLL; the pressures and part mass stay article-specific because those the sim really does differentiate. --- 2026-09-20 WELLE-A / CAPT-REZEPT, EVERY ROW NOW NAMES THE SIGNAL IT CONSTRAINS. This file is `parked: true` and is therefore skipped by the resolvers entirely, but its `parameters[]` was also INCOMPLETE in a way that would bite the day it is un-parked, and that is the day nobody is looking: 1 of its 7 rows carried neither `smAttribute` nor `constraintId`. `smAttribute` is what names the sm_attribute the engine aggregates on the edge, and `constraintId` is the PRIMARY half of the constraint<->ref mapping the it-evaluator builds (recipe-band-resolver.ts indexProfiles: `if (p.constraintId && p.valueFrom) refByConstraint.set(...)`) — without them the resolver falls back to a derivation and the UI has no row key at all. Both are filled in now from the profile's own constraint list, for every row that a constraint judges. THE `resin` ROW IS A PARAMETER, NOT A NOTE, AND IT KEEPS NO BAND. It was the one row here with no `smAttribute`, and the tempting reading was that it is a material remark that does not belong in `parameters[]`. It is not: profiles/machines/injection-molding-machine.json publishes `resin` as a String attribute, the machine really emits it (machines-sgm derives it from the nozzle setpoint, config.ts resinForNozzleTemp), and recipe-schema.json provides for exactly this case — 'a nominal can be CATEGORICAL (e.g. param resin, soll PA66-GF30) ... those parameters are documentation and carry no band'. So it gets `smAttribute: resin` and stays band-less: it is a row the setter must see and a value the engine can compare, but not a tolerance, and inventing a numeric band for it would be the opposite of the fix. Consumers already handle the categorical case (recipe-source-kit getSoll returns undefined, never 0, for a non-numeric soll). NO control limits are added to this file: the resolvers fall through PER REF to the less specific equipment-scoped recipe when a file does not declare one (recipe-source-kit getValues / it-evaluator resolveFromBindings), so recipe-sgm-004-default.json's warn/action tiers already cover a run under this recipe, and a second copy here would be a second place to drift. --- CAPT-LEAD 2026-09-20: hotrunner control limits ADDED. Until today this article recipe declared the hotrunner TOLERANCE [288.5, 301.5] but no control limits, and an article recipe WINS over sgm-004-default when its article runs. So for exactly the two articles this machine actually produces, the hot runner had no WARN and no ACTION: it could drift out of the band without anything ever escalating - the same failure class as the mouldTempC gap, one level down and harder to see, because the default recipe right next to it looks complete. The values are NOT new numbers: same machine, same attribute, same tolerance as sgm-004-default, therefore the same limits. ACTION is the tolerance boundary itself - a control limit that stops the line must never sit inside the specification - and WARN is tolerance minus 2 sigma, sigma = 1.50 degC measured on .120 over the shipped DEFAULT_CONFIG (n = 79,200 samples at 1 Hz, mean 294.995 on sgm-04). NOT added here: peak/hold pressure bands and a part-mass band for sgm-005/006, because neither can be DERIVED today - sgm-004's own peak band [450, 560] does not follow from injectionPressureBar 1000 through the published model (peak = currentPressureBar x 1.05), both machines are idle so it cannot be measured either, and a band that is invented STOPS a machine. See audits/2026-09-20/ in the sim-v5 repo.
parkedReason:
PARKED — this recipe can NEVER match a production order, and it has never matched one. MEASURED 2026-07-12 against the FULL article master of sim-v5 PROD (.154): 222 articles, population exhausted. match.article "housing-A" DOES NOT EXIST among them. The ERP keys its articles as PART-A/B/C, WIP-*, RAW-*, _V4_*. Consequence: match never fires, the bands never resolve, and NOTHING is ever checked against this recipe — silently. It has been shipped as if it were monitoring sgm-004 since it was written. It was not. The only recipe that actually binds sgm-004 is recipe-sgm-004-default.json, which matches on equipment (sgm-004), not on article.

WHY IT IS PARKED AND NOT REPAIRED: repairing it means naming the article this recipe is FOR, and that is a product decision, not an inference. Plausible candidates exist — "PART-A" (FINISHED, "Gehaeuseoberteil komplett (Premium)") and "WIP-HOUSING-BASE" (WIP, "Gehaeuseboden unbearbeitet (Rohteil von SGM-01)") — but picking one on resemblance would be inventing a fact about the customer's product. A wrong article is worse than a parked recipe: it would silently apply PA66-GF30 bands to the wrong part and then look like it was working.

PRECONDITION TO UN-PARK: set match.article to an article_no that exists in SMProfile-Article, confirmed by the product owner. ci/check-vocab-drift.mjs then verifies it against the live article master on every run and FAILS (exit 1) if it ever goes dead again. Un-parking without that check passing is not allowed.
